The failing test `testHeaderMissingWithNull()` creates a CSV parser with a specific format, including setting a null string to empty ("") and enabling headers while ignoring empty headers. This test triggers a `NullPointerException`.

Looking at the `CSVFormat` class, the `DEFAULT` format is initialized with default values. The test then customizes this format by enabling headers and setting a null string to empty using the `withHeader()` and `withNullString("")` methods, respectively.

The issue in the test occurs because when both the null string is set to empty and an empty header value is present, a `NullPointerException` is thrown. This indicates a potential bug in handling empty header values along with an empty null string.

To fix this issue, the `CSVFormat` class should be updated to handle the case of an empty header value and an empty null string properly.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed based on the diagnosis.
```
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.withHeader(java.lang.String...)
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.withNullString(java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
